newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FORECAST-Cheung Kong may use CKI gains to boost net.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Cheung Kong may use CKI gains to boost net.

text.p: After a slow year for property sales, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd may use an exceptional gain from last year's spinoff of its infrastructure arm to boost its 1996 earnings, analysts said on Friday.
"I am looking for a 20 percent increase (in net profit)," said David Low, research manager at Asia Equity.
"The bulk of that is from an exceptional of HK$1.5 billion from the flotation of CKI last year. That is essentially it. Last year they did not actually sell many projects," he said.
Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) listed in Hong Kong last July.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) is due to report its results for calendar 1996 next Wednesday. It had net profit of HK$11.13 billion in 1995.

The Hong Kong property developer's interim earnings growth of 37 percent to HK$8.16 billion beat market expectations after Cheung Kong booked profits from its major projects during the first half of the year.
"We are looking for 9.5 percent core earnings growth to about HK$12.19 billion," said Carol Lai, research manager at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"It was quite an uneventful year for Cheung Kong. There were not many main projects which were launched in 1996," she said.
Cheung Kong sold units at its Kingswood Villas project in Yuen Long, Laguna City in Kowloon and University Heights in Pokfulam.
"Those are the only residential projects launched," said Lai. She expected development profits of HK$5.9 billion in 1996, "which is actually quite low".
Lai said an exceptional profit of HK$1.5 billion from the CKI spinoff could boost the net figure to HK$13.7 billion.
In a major reshuffle of the Cheung Kong group, announced in January, Cheung Kong said it would transfer its 70.66 percent stake in CKI to its associate Hutchison Whampoa Ltd.
It said the estimated surplus on the transfer of the stake and the 1996 flotation of CKI amounted to HK$9.63 billion.
CKI posted 1996 net profit of HK$886 million on Thursday.
Vickers Ballas property analyst Desmond Cheung forecast profit of HK$12.4 billion at Cheung Kong, which did not include an exceptional gain from the CKI spinoff.
He said property sales would contribute 40-45 percent, Hutchison Whampoa 30 percent and rentals five to eight percent.
He said 1996 "was satisfactory, but the major boost will be in 1997".
Sales at Laguna Verde, Kingswood Villa and Maywood Court should bring substantial profits this year, analysts said.
"We are looking for something like HK$14.3 billion (net profit) in 1997," said Cheung.
